items.title: Binance hit by the largest crypto theft on record
items.what: On 29 October, attackers took about $6.4 billion from Binance hot wallets on around ten blockchains in roughly 20 minutes, including about 18,270 BTC. Blockchain analytics firms and the FBI attribute the attack to a North Korean group. Binance suspended withdrawals, says it will absorb the losses rather than its users, and began reopening withdrawals on 1 November.
items.why: Coins held on a platform are a claim on that platform. Even the largest exchange can pause withdrawals for days. Where your keys sit, and what you would do during such a pause, is part of your plan.

items.title: Quantum risk moves from research papers to boardrooms
items.what: On 30 October, the board of a Nasdaq-listed company approved a plan to sell or pledge its 5,833 BTC, citing the Binance hack and quantum computing risk. Research published this year lowered the estimated machine size needed to break Bitcoin's signatures about 20-fold, although today's machines remain far from it. BIP-360, a proposal for a quantum-resistant address type, is in Bitcoin's proposal repository with no activation date.
items.why: The risk concerns coins whose public key is already visible on the blockchain, mainly old and reused addresses. It is a long-term protocol topic, debated openly. Avoiding address reuse is a habit you control today.

items.title: Strategy reports its quarter: 848,517 BTC on the balance sheet
items.what: On 29 October, Strategy, the largest listed holder of Bitcoin, reported third-quarter results driven by the change in value of its holdings, and announced that its CFO is leaving on 5 November.
items.why: Under fair-value accounting, the profits of Bitcoin treasury companies swing with the Bitcoin price, in both directions. A share in such a company is exposure to the company, its debt and its decisions, not Bitcoin itself.
